newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian state chief to write to Mahathir on race.
newsitem.headline: Australian state chief to write to Mahathir on race.

text.p: The leader of the Australian state of Victoria said on Tuesday he would write to Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad offering to investigate reports of a Malaysian student being racially abused in Melbourne.

"I certainly intend writing to the (Malaysian) Prime Minister indicating that if he wants to provide any further information we will certainly do our best to follow it up," Premier Jeff Kennett told reporters.
Kennett said such incidents were not widespread and urged the media not to overreact.
"This is not something that we accept. It is certainly not something that we tolerate when it is brought to our attention," he said.
Mahathir said on Monday Malaysia might recall its students from Australia if the reported racist threats against them were found to be serious.

The national Bernama news agency reported on Sunday that a Malaysian student leader in Australia wanted the Malaysian and Australian governments to protect foreign students from racial abuse and threats.

She was quoted by Bernama as saying that several Malaysian students had had "nasty experiences" such as verbal abuse, since Australia was engulfed in a race row sparked by independent politician Pauline Hanson.
Hanson, in her maiden parliamentary speech in September, said Australia was being swamped by Asians and called for an immediate moratorium on immigration.
A 22-year-old Malaysian student recently told reporters in Malaysia she was racially abused by two Australians who were alleged to have told her to get out of their country.
Kennett invited the student to contact either him directly or the state's Multicultural Commission with details of the abuse.
"I think Dr Mahathir, like most adults, would want to know what the facts were," he said.
Asians make up about five percent of Australia's 18 million population.
More than 11,000 Malaysians are studying in Australia.
